newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA'S CONGRESS PARTY PREPARES FOR A COMEBACK.
newsitem.headline: INDIA'S CONGRESS PARTY PREPARES FOR A COMEBACK.

text.p: India's beleaguered Congress party on Friday launched a scathing attack on Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's fractious coalition and said it alone could provide stability to the nation.

"When elections come after one or one-and-a-half years, your leader will hoist the national flag on the Red Fort," Congress President Sitaram Kesri said in his inaugural speech at the party's plenary session.
The historic Red Fort is the traditional venue where the country's prime minister unfurls the national flag on Independence Day on August 15.
Congress party provides crucial support for Gujral's ruling United Front coalition but holds no government portfolios.

"Today we are supporting the government at the centre, but the dignity of the Congress will always be protected," said Kesri, who was cheered furiously by party workers who had flocked to the indoor stadium where the session was held.

The 112-year-old party began its three-day, 80th plenary session in the eastern city of Calcutta, which wore a festive look. Large, colourful cutouts of Congress leaders and freedom fighters adorned the streets and loudspeakers blared patriotic songs.
Congress has ruled India for all but five years since independence from British rule in 1947, but has been repeatedly stung by scandals and was thrown out of power in last year's polls.
Congress leaders said Gujral's 15-party United Front coalition lacked cohesion, was weak and failed to fulfil the aspirations of the common people.
"To keep India united and secular, only Congress can serve the purpose," said senior party leader K. Karunakaran.
"A 15-party coalition at the centre is not worth it."
"Coalition politics has not paid dividends," senior Congress leader Sharad Pawar told Reuters on Thursday. "But we will continue to support the Gujral government."
Congress leaders reassured the United Front of its support, but warned that its backing should not be taken for granted.
"It is not forever," said Karunakaran.
"The Congress is the glue, the bonding adhesive, that holds the polity of this country together," said a resolution moved on 50 years of the nation's independence.
Kesri also did not spare the regional parties that form the core of the United Front's coalition, saying growing regionalism threatened the social and political fabric of the nation.
Karunakaran said the party looked to Sonia Gandhi, the Italian-born widow of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, to take an active interest and strengthen the organisation.
Gandhi, a political recluse who became a member of the party in March, was expected to arrive later on Friday and attend the plenary session.
The party was scheduled to adopt resolutions on crucial political, economic and international issues at its three-day meeting.
The economic resolution moved by former finance minister Manmohan Singh pledged the party's support for economic reforms but called for policies that would alleviate poverty.
"Growth is meaningful only if it helps to raise the living standards of the poor," said Singh.
